purpose: Provider-neutral deployment specification for the Valorant Analytics Platform (apps/web) — TASK-049 section 20. This is a description of how a release bundle is intended to be deployed by a future provider-specific task. It is not itself a provider deployment config and triggers no deployment on its own.

application.workingDirectory: repository root (application lives at apps/web, run via pnpm --filter)

runtimePackage.refreshPolicy: Refreshed independently of an application deploy/rebuild — never baked into the application image or build output.

shutdownBehavior: Standard Next.js/Node SIGTERM handling: the process should be given a grace period to finish in-flight requests before a forced kill. No background jobs, timers, schedulers, or open database connections exist in this stack that require special drain handling.
releaseVersionReporting: The readiness endpoint's sourceMode/runtimePackageVersion/currentModelVersion fields, combined with the release bundle's own release-manifest.json, are the source of truth for which release/runtime-package pair is actually running.

rollbackInputs.previousReleaseManifestPath: A saved copy of a prior release's own release-manifest.json (see operations/rollback-runbook.md).

edgeRuntime.reason: Every route under apps/web/src/app/api/internal/prediction/** declares `export const runtime = "nodejs"` and depends on node:fs/promises, node:crypto, node:path — none of which exist on the Edge runtime. Statically audited by apps/web/src/app/api/internal/prediction/nodeRuntime.test.ts.

notes: This file is a specification, not an executable deployment config — it makes no network request and triggers no deployment.
No credentials, secrets, or provider-specific tokens are referenced anywhere in this file.
Provider-specific integration (a Dockerfile build, a serverless function packaging step, an actual hosting target) remains future work — see docs/37, 'Known limitations'.
